How does a model change reach a following deployment, with and without Git?

Long image

A

Answer

The designer changes the model on the authoring deployment and fixes versions. A following deployment never replays those edits: a Migration moves it. Its jump takes the target model from the version itself: a frozen snapshot without Git, the tag's checkout with Git.

  1. The jump is the model half of a run. Steps before and after it change data.1
  2. Without Git, the jump rewrites the model to the frozen to version with createEntity, alterEntityAttribute and instance writes on model.2
  3. With Git, the jump checks the tag out and reloads the model: the files carry the model, so no model action runs.3
  4. The epic chose this over replaying the traced model actions, because a replayed createEntity empties existing storage on three stores.1

Applies toLibrary example of epic #694, section 5, against the code on _integration after #9 (#739, #740, #742). Rollback (#709) and the clone installer (#710) are not built yet.

1

Without Git: what happens on each deployment?

Diagram structure
  • Freeze 1.0.0 ifreeze1
  • Add Book.isbn iedit
  • Freeze 1.1.0 ifreeze2
  • Generate migration igen
  • Install 1.0.0 iinstall
  • Expand steps iexpand
  • Jump to 1.1.0 ijump
  • Fill isbn ifill
  • State at 1.1.0 istate
  • iedit → ifreeze2 · trace record
  • iexpand → ijump
  • ifill → istate
  • ifreeze1 → iedit
  • ifreeze2 → igen
  • igen → iinstall · shared modelVersion
  • iinstall → iexpand · runMigration
  • ijump → ifill
  1. Freeze 1.0.0 ↗

    Snapshots every model element into modelVersion and adds a version marker to the trace records.

  2. Add Book.isbn ↗

    The commit updates the Book Entity row and writes one trace record.

  3. Generate migration ↗

    Replays the records on 1.0.0 and checks they give 1.1.0. The draft lists the change and an empty fill step.

  4. Install 1.0.0 ↗

    The following deployment is created at a version: the model is rewritten to the frozen 1.0.0.

  5. Jump to 1.1.0 ↗

    Rewrites the model to the frozen 1.1.0: alterEntityAttribute adds the isbn column, then the Book row is updated.

  6. Fill isbn ↗

    The designer's data step computes isbn for existing books.

The two deployments share only the modelVersion storage: versions, records and Migrations.4

2

With Git: what changes?

Diagram structure
  • Commit, tag 1.0.0 gtag1
  • Add Book.isbn, commit gedit
  • Generate, commit it ggen
  • Tag 1.1.0 gtag2
  • Clone at 1.0.0 gat
  • Read Migration at 1.1.0 gread
  • Jump: checkout 1.1.0 gjump
  • Fill isbn gfill
  • State at 1.1.0 gstate
  • gat → gread · runMigration
  • gedit → ggen · trace file
  • gfill → gstate
  • ggen → gtag2
  • gjump → gfill
  • gread → gjump · after expand
  • gtag1 → gedit
  • gtag2 → gat · fetch
  1. Generate, commit it ↗

    Reads tag 1.0.0 and HEAD, writes the Migration file; it is committed before the tag, so version 1.1.0 holds its own Migration.

  2. Read Migration at 1.1.0 ↗

    The runner reads it from the tag's commit without a checkout and copies it into the state record.

  3. Jump: checkout 1.1.0 ↗

    Checks out refs/tags/1.1.0 and reloads; the model files change on disk, no model action runs.

  4. Fill isbn ↗

    Writes data, which sits in a folder Git ignores, so the checkout never touches it.

Section 5.2 puts the data outside the clone (D7); #9 uses a gitignored folder inside it until the installer of #710 exists.5

3

What exactly is the jump?

The epic defines it in D2-d, not in its vocabulary: the jump brings the model to the target version, between the expand and the fill steps.1

Without GitWith Git
Source of the target modelFrozen *Version rows of toFiles at the tag to
What runsapplyModelState: model actions and instance writes, marked as the run'sgitAction_checkout, then a reload
Model actions issuedcreateEntity for an added Entity, alterEntityAttribute for an added attribute, create, update and delete of model rowsNone
Storage of removed elementsKept, for a contract stepKept
Storage of added elementsYesCreated by the model actionsGapNot created; works for filesystem data, not tested on SQL
Epic planRestore action (D6, #709) plus add-only reconciliationCheckout plus Q31 check plus reconciliation
In #9Restore built underneath, reconciliation set aside (N5)Checkout and reload only

The same jump installs a new following deployment at its first version.6

4

So should a run allow model actions?

Yes: model actions are how the model migrates, and without Git a run does issue them. The jump derives them from the frozen to version, so the model ends exactly at to. The question is only whether a hand-written step may issue more of them.

Where a model action could come fromEffect on the following modelStatus
The jump, derived from the to snapshotExactModel equals toBuilt (#9)
An expand step, before the jumpOverwritten by the jumpAllowed today without Git
A fill or contract step, after the jumpDivergesModel differs from to, while the state says toAllowed today without Git
Replaying the traced actions instead of a jump (D2-a)Model reaches to; a replayed createEntity empties its storage on SQL, IndexedDB and MongoDBRejected by the epic
Any step, with GitBlocks the next checkout, since it edits tracked filesRefused

The choice for #741

Keep D2-d: the jump owns every model write, steps change data, and a run refuses model actions in steps in both settings. Or let steps hold model actions without Git, and accept that a run can end with a model other than to.
